episodes.215464: Modest monsoon moisture combined with daytime heating under a strong area of high pressure resulted in thunderstorm development over the high terrain during the afternoon hours of August 20th. Storms moved into nearby lower elevations across central New Mexico during the late afternoon and early evening hours. One storm resulted in some arroyo and urban flash flooding in east central and southeast Albuquerque due to rainfall amounts of 0.50 to 1.25 inches in just under an hour. One person ended up being rescued with another person swept away due to flash flooding in the Tramway Channel. Storms tapered off after sunset due to the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.215476: As a front moved through Middle Tennessee on August 20, 2026, it helped to develop scattered thunderstorms across southern portions of the area that evening. Across Lawrence County, these thunderstorms produced damaging winds which downed a few trees across the county.
episodes.215807: Three rounds of thunderstorm activity occurred from late on August 20 through the evening of August 22. One decaying MCS crossed into northeastern Central Alabama early on August 21, causing scattered tree damage across Cherokee, Etowah, and St. Clair counties. Scattered activity occurred during the evening of the 21st, including in Barbour, Marengo, and Tallapoosa counties. The third round came on the evening of the 22nd, with another MCS moving down the I-22 corridor through Marion, Fayette, and Walker counties, weakening below severe limits before reaching the Birmingham metro area.
episodes.215956: Isolated thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the late afternoon into the early evening on Friday (8/21).  The strongest storm produced penny size hail as it tracked through central Wisconsin.
episodes.216045: A weak shortwave trough along with deep instability, dry air aloft, and significant low level moisture combined to produce robust thunderstorms across eastern GA. Widespread wind damage from downbursts occurred across the CSRA as a result.
episodes.216046: A weak shortwave trough along with deep instability, dry air aloft, and significant low level moisture combined to produce robust thunderstorms across South Carolina. Widespread wind damage from downbursts occurred across the central SC as a result included several isolated areas of concentrated microburst damage.
episodes.216227: A cold front stalled along the Crystal Coast of Eastern North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours of August twenty-first. As this occurred, a weak wave of low pressure rode along this stalled boundary and was the focal point for scattered showers and thunderstorms across Eastern North Carolina. As instability increased with peak heating during the afternoon and evening hours, a few of these thunderstorms became severe in nature bringing a strong wind threat to portions of the Crystal Coast waters and the southern Pamlico Sound.
episodes.216292: Thunderstorms developed along a prefrontal trough in the coastal plain early in the afternoon hours. Several storms became severe and produced wind damage.
episodes.216318: A cold front tracked through the forecast area and produced flash flooding.
episodes.216419: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northwest and north central Illinois from late afternoon through late evening producing isolated hail and one brief tornado.
episodes.216436: A cold front moved from the NW to SE across Minnesota with a threat for severe weather mostly across the central portion of the state. However, enhanced clearing across southwest MN led to efficient atmospheric recovery from precipitation that had moved through earlier in the day. By the early evening, storms redeveloped along the frontal boundary and moved into a buoyant sheared airmass. This resulted in isolated cells to feature rotating updrafts and produce quarter to tennis ball size hail across portions of southwestern MN. ||The tennis ball size hail stone (2.5 diameter) was measured near the border of Yellow Medicine and Redwood Counties or 4 miles NE of Vesta.
episodes.216474: A long-track supercell moved north to south across the western Nebraska Panhandle from Chadron down through Sidney. Tornadic rotation was seen on radar, with reports coming in of a potential tornado. another isolated storm moved from Guernsey to Scottsbluff, dropping severe hail. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 612.
episodes.216559: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 21st, as warm, moist, and unstable air was forced over a stationary frontal boundary by a low level jet. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to quarter size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216591: An approaching trough of low pressure across the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley region aided the development of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Storms initially developed over South Carolina and eastern portions of North Carolina, but grew in coverage and strength across central North Carolina in the afternoon and evening hours. Numerous damaging wind reports were observed, along with isolated flash flooding.
episodes.216801: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe. In addition, an area of slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding in and near Dothan.

episodes.217603: On Thursday, August 20, 2026, an advancing frontal system triggered scattered rounds of severe thunderstorms across north-central and northeastern Minnesota. As these cells intensified during the late afternoon and evening, they produced frequent lightning and numerous reports of quarter- to half-dollar-sized hail across counties including Cass, Crow Wing, Aitkin, and Itasca. Communities such as Boy River, Remer, and areas near Crosslake and Silica were directly hit by localized hail swaths and brief downpours. In addition to the hail activity, gusty downdrafts knocked down trees and caused minor home damage near Brainerd before storms tracked further south and east.
episodes.217618: Scattered strong thunderstorms developed just ahead of a cold front. Several funnel clouds were reported.
episodes.217680: A cold front began to sink into the Mid-South late in the evening on the 20th. South of the TN/MS stateline, thunderstorms were able to dip into enough instability ahead of this front for a swath of robust convection to form. Large trees were downed across northern Mississippi.
episodes.217724: A weak quasi-stationary mid-level boundary extending from central Mississippi down to coastal Mississippi and Alabama served as a focusing mechanism for a broken line of storms to form across the Pine Belt region of Mississippi in the late afternoon and early evening hours.  These storms then moved to the south-southwest and produced localized damaging wind gusts in coastal and southwest Mississippi.
episodes.217726: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere.  Additionally, a weak mid-level trough axis extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama.   A mesoscale convective complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the mid-level boundary over central Mississippi and then swept southward through southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi during the afternoon and early evening hours.  The severe storms within the larger convective complex produced severe wind gusts and hail in the region.
episodes.217727: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a weak mid-level trough axis extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama. A mesoscale convective complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the mid-level boundary over central Mississippi and then swept southward through southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi during the afternoon and early evening hours. The severe storms within the larger convective complex produced severe wind gusts and hail in the region.
episodes.217728: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a weak mid-level trough axis extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama. A mesoscale convective complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the mid-level boundary over central Mississippi and then swept southward through portions of the coastal waters in the late afternoon and early evening hours. The severe storms within the larger convective complex produced severe marine thunderstorm wind gusts in Lake Pontchartrain and the Gulf waters off the coast of Louisiana.
episodes.217823: On August 18th, weak shortwave energy moved through the eastern periphery of the Heat Wave ridge over a moist and unstable airmass enhancing storms mainly over northeast and central Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes with stronger storms, capable of wet microbursts, pulsing along mesoscale boundary collisions in the afternoon into evening. On August 19-20, a frontal boundary stalled over southern Georgia as ���Heat Wave��� ridging built in from the west. Tropical moisture of 2+ inches of precipitable water remained south of the front, mainly over northeast Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes. The combination of high moisture, strong diurnal heating, and sea breeze/outflow interactions supported strong to severe storms capable of producing damaging winds, frequent lightning strikes and torrential downpours. Weak steering flow allowed for localized flooding. On August 22nd, lingering upper shortwaves ahead of the weakening frontal boundary in central Georgia triggered morning showers and isolated storms moving inland from the Gulf. Convection then spread east-northeastward through the day in the general southwest flow. A few stronger storms occurred along sea breeze boundary mergers in the late morning to early afternoon hours in north-central Florida.
episodes.217938: A severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Roseau County MN during the afternoon hours.
episodes.218021: During the afternoon hours of August 21st, a storm brough strong wind gusts to southern Cass County near Archie.
episodes.218022: During the afternoon and evening hours of August 21st, storms brought damaging wind gusts to portions of eastern Kansas.
episodes.218059: A Thunderstorm complex moved in from Southwestern Nebraska, moving south through Western Kansas. This complex produced multiple thunderstorm gusts, hail and damage reports.  The peak gust of 83 mph was measured at the Oakley airport.  The largest hail stone reported was golfball size, falling in Rawlins and Decatur counties.
episodes.218060: A thunderstorm complex moved in from Southwestern Nebraska, moving south through Western Kansas. This complex produced multiple thunderstorm gusts, hail and damage reports.  The largest hailstone of two inches was reported in McCook, along with the strongest wind gust of 60 mph.
episodes.218124: A trough entering the eastern half of the CONUS with several embedded shortwaves rounding its base along with a slow-moving surface front approaching the region from the west and northwest encountering a modestly unstable airmass with deep moisture, supported thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.218167: During the late afternoon and early evening hours on August 20th, thunderstorms quickly developed along and near a stationary boundary draped across Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. Along and south of the boundary, temperatures soared near 105 degrees with lower to middle 60s dewpoints, resulting in a strongly unstable air mass. This activity was largely displaced from a mid-level trough and more enhanced flow aloft moving across the lower Ohio Valley, limiting the overall scope of convective organization. Nevertheless, near 25 knots of mid-level northwesterly flow oriented perpendicular to the stationary boundary and evolving thunderstorms supported a more loosely organized cluster of storms capable of producing locally damaging wind gusts. As a result, several reports of wind damage were recorded across parts of Southwest Arkansas.
episodes.218170: During the afternoon on August 21st, a late summer cold front extended from northern Mississippi westward along the Arkansas/Louisiana border and into northeastern Texas. This boundary, along with remnant outflow from overnight convection, the coastal sea breeze and a remnant MCV, served as a focus for convective initiation in the afternoon amid a hot and humid air mass with temperatures in the upper 90s and dew points in the mid 70s. While effective shear was quite meager, modestly stronger low-to-mid level flow, high precipitable water (PW) values near 1.75-2.0+ inches and steepening low-level lapse rates near 8-9+ degrees C/km, all combined to support scattered damaging severe wind gusts with water-loaded downbursts. As a result, several damaging wind reports were recorded across parts of North Central Louisiana.
episodes.218171: During the afternoon on August 21st, a late summer cold front extended from northern Mississippi westward along the Arkansas/Louisiana border and into northeastern Texas. This boundary, along with remnant outflow from overnight convection, the coastal sea breeze and a remnant MCV, served as a focus for convective initiation in the afternoon amid a hot and humid air mass with temperatures in the upper 90s and dew points in the mid 70s. While effective shear was quite meager, modestly stronger low-to-mid level flow, high precipitable water (PW) values near 1.75-2.0+ inches and steepening low-level lapse rates near 8-9+ degrees C/km, all combined to support scattered damaging severe wind gusts with water-loaded downbursts. As a result, several damaging wind reports were recorded across parts of Deep East Texas.
episodes.218222: On August 21st and 22nd, a mid level shortwave moved through southeast Georgia and interacted with sea breeze and outflow boundaries to produce scattered to numerous showers and storms. Cooler than normal temperatures aloft from -7C to -8C at 500 mb increased mid level lapse rates which supported a couple of strong to severe thunderstorms. Another frontal boundary dropped southward into northern GA on the 23rd, into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells.
episodes.218227: A heat wave developed across the region during late August. A weak boundary and short wave approached from the north causing strong to severe storms.
episodes.218283: Several rounds of storms resulted in isolated instances of flooding across the Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.218284: A very warm and unstable airmass was in place across the Mid-Atlantic on August 20. A disturbance aloft passed by to the north but was able to spark several rounds of strong storms across Virginia with strong winds and frequent lightning.
episodes.218290: A slow moving cold front dropped southeast through the day, with a few storms igniting along the boundary south of Interstate 90. With up to 2000-2500 J/kg MLCAPE and deep-layer shear of 35 to 45 knots, storms remained isolated and were briefly supercellular with hail up to golf ball size and winds up to around 75 mph. An isolated tornado occurred with a more western storm with some property damage.
episodes.218388: Scattered thunderstorms moved southeast from North Carolina into upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of these storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in northern Spartanburg County.
episodes.218416: Isolated thunderstorms fueled by high instability and large amounts of downdraft potential energy produced a couple bouts of hail and damaging winds.
episodes.218497: Scattered thunderstorms and multiple storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the evening along and ahead of a cold front. Several of the storms produced localized damaging wind gusts as well as isolated large hail.
episodes.218501: A cluster of thunderstorms moved into northeast Georgia during the pre-dawn hours in association with a cold front. A small area of wind damage was reported in Rabun County.
episodes.218502: A cluster of thunderstorms moved over the North Carolina foothills during the morning in association with a cold front. Strong wind gusts caused some damage in Burke County.
episodes.218505: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms and storm clusters developed along a cold front from mid-afternoon into early evening. Several of the storms produced large hail and/or locally damaging wind gusts across the foothills and Piedmont.
episodes.218509: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across the Piedmont and upstate of South Carolina during the evening in association with a cold front. Several of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.

A very slow moving tornado developed around 3 miles south-southwest of Olivet west of 425th Avenue and just north of 289th Street. The tornado moved to the southeast across 425th Avenue and into a farmstead on the northeast quadrant of the intersection of the two roads. The tornado rolled a camper and a public video showed the removal of roof panels on outbuildings. The tornado dissipated along 289th Street just east of the farmstead. The tornado was rated EF0 with a peak estimated wind speed of 80 mph. The average path width was 25 yards.

A brief tornado with estimated peak winds of 70 mph touched down in a farm field east of the intersection of Henkel Road and Route 51 and caused damage to crops. The tornado moved generally southward and caused damage to several roofs of buildings near the intersection of Cedar Grove Road and Route 52. Additional damage to crops occurred. The tornado ended in a field to the north of Pike Creek west of Route 52. The entire life cycle of this tornado was captured by several storm chasers. Drone footage from local law enforcement was used to determine the path of this tornado.
